help.label: Explanation
help.level: Level declared by the pilot. Weems does not check it.
help.distance: Sum of the distances along the recorded tracks, shown flights only. Around the Earth at the equator: 21,600 nm.
help.map: One arc per route, thicker when flown often, in the colour of the aircraft category most flown on it. Airports are placed at the first and last recorded point of each flight.
help.activity: Flight hours by month of departure (UTC). An empty month is still shown.
help.takeoffs: Takeoffs by day of the week and hour, in the local time of the departure airport. The darker the cell, the more takeoffs.
help.flights: Finished flights the pilot chose to show. Flights in progress and hidden flights do not count.
help.hours: Flight time: from takeoff to the last touchdown, pauses excluded. Block time: from engine start or pushback to stopping at the gate.
help.dayNight: Night as defined by the regulations (EASA): sun more than 6° below the horizon. Computed at the aircraft's position, at every moment of the flight.
help.longest: The flight with the longest block time.
help.streak: Weeks in a row (Monday to Sunday, UTC) with at least one finished and shown flight.
help.airports: Different departure and arrival airports, over all shown flights.
help.aircraft: Different aircraft by ICAO type (A20N, B738…), or by their simulator name when the type is unknown.
help.clean: Final landings with a single touchdown, no bounce and no go-around.
help.average: Vertical speed at the first contact of the final landing (after any go-around), averaged over the flights where it was measured, for all aircraft then by category: a firm touchdown does not mean the same in a C172 and in a 787.
help.best: The softest final landing of each flown category: the touchdown vertical speed closest to zero. A single record for all aircraft favoured light aircraft.
help.experience: Airborne hours (wheels off the ground) of the finished, shown flights, sorted by the aircraft's ICAO type. When the type is unknown, Weems estimates the category from the engine and weight given by the simulator.
help.engines: Same columns as the EASA logbook: single-engine (SE) and multi-engine (ME), from the number of engines given by the simulator.

meta.title: Discover Weems · How it works
meta.description: A tracker records your MSFS flights, the site tells their story, the community sees them go by, and you improve flight after flight.

banner.title: Fly, understand, improve.
banner.slogan: A tracker records every flight you make in the simulator. The site tells their story, the community sees them go by, and you improve flight after flight.

tracker.title: A tracker you forget about
tracker.text: Install it once. It recognises MSFS 2020 and 2024, records your flight from engine start and splits it into 12 phases, from taxi to parking.
tracker.point1: Nothing to fill in, nothing to start in flight
tracker.point2: The flight is kept if the connection drops, and sent when it is back
tracker.point3: A window shows the state of the simulator and the flight

followUp.title: Every flight, told
followUp.text: As soon as you land, your flight is in your logbook: route on the map, altitude profile, phases, landing and flight log.
followUp.point2: Your friends follow your flight live

community.title: Fly alone, never isolated
community.text: Your flight shows on the live map, next to the other pilots' flights. Your public profile shows your hours, routes and aircraft, to share wherever you like.
community.point2: Public profile to share, private until you publish it
community.point3: Coming soon: virtual airlines and their pilots

simplicity.title: Simple from the first flight
simplicity.text: An account, the tracker, and you fly. No flight plan to file, no setting to figure out.
simplicity.point1: Free to fly, no flight limit
simplicity.point2: One account for the site and the tracker
simplicity.point3: In French and English, light or dark

training.title: Fly like a real crew
training.text: Weems reviews each flight with airline pilots' benchmarks: stabilised approach, 250 kt below FL100, passenger comfort. It shows you what went well and what to work on.
training.point3: Bank angle and g-load felt in the cabin

progress.title: See how far you have come
progress.text: Hours by aircraft category, average touchdown, regularity: you see your progress flight after flight, and set yourself goals.
progress.point3: You and the community, by aircraft category

notice.title: For simulation only.
notice.text: Weems does not replace aviation training and is never used for a real flight.

closing.title: Every flight counts.
closing.text: Make each one a step closer to the pilot you want to become.

meta.title: Features
meta.description: Every Weems feature, from the MSFS tracker to running a virtual airline, and the plan that includes each one.

Features.title: Everything Weems does
Features.lead: From your first recorded flight to running an airline: every feature, what it brings you and the plan that includes it.

groups.fly: Install the tracker and fly in MSFS: every flight is recorded and shown live, with nothing to type.
groups.logbook: Your personal logbook, filled in by itself, with all the data of every flight.
groups.analysis: Understand what happened and improve, flight after flight, with benchmarks taken from the regulations.
groups.company: Create a virtual airline, recruit pilots, approve their flights and run your rankings.

tracker.title: MSFS 2020 and 2024 tracker
tracker.text: A small Windows app that connects to the simulator, detects departure and arrival and sends the flight, even if the connection drops on the way.

liveMap.title: Live flight map
liveMap.text: Every pilot in the air on a real-time map: route flown, progress, active airports, search.

publicProfile.title: Public profile
publicProfile.text: A page in your name to share: hours, distance, aircraft, latest flights. You choose what is public.

flightHistory.title: Full history
flightHistory.text: All your flights are kept, with no limit on number or age, free plan included.

simbriefNextFlight.title: Next SimBrief flight
simbriefNextFlight.text: Your SimBrief flight plan shows in the logbook; one button starts the tracker ready to go.

logbookSummary.title: Logbook summary
logbookSummary.text: At a glance: last flight, hours this month, average touchdown and consistency calendar.

flightDetail.title: Flight sheet
flightDetail.text: For each flight: route on the map, altitude profile, landing and phase timeline.

flightBands.title: Flight bands
flightBands.text: Altitude, speed, vertical speed, bank, g, thrust, flaps, gear, autopilot… plotted over the whole flight.

flightNotes.title: Notes and tags
flightNotes.text: A private note and tags on each flight, to find an exercise or a route again.

basicStats.title: Basic statistics
basicStats.text: Hours, touchdowns, flying days and hours, routes, aircraft, airports and distance flown.

statsPeriod.title: Statistics period
statsPeriod.text: Statistics cover the last months on the free plan, your whole career with Pilot Pro.

workOnBasic.title: “To work on”
workOnBasic.text: Bounces, alerts and go-arounds spotted on your latest flights, so you know what to practise.

goals.title: Goals
goals.text: Set yourself a goal (hours, soft touchdowns, consistency) and follow its progress.

approachAnalysis.title: Approach analysis
approachAnalysis.text: Speed, vertical speed and centreline at 1,000 and 500 ft, flare, touchdown zone: was your approach stabilised?

workOnDetailed.title: Detailed “To work on”
workOnDetailed.text: Each weak point in detail: long flare, speed out of tolerance at 500 ft…

flightBandsMarks.title: Marks on the bands
flightBandsMarks.text: Moments worth a second look are marked on the bands: high sink rate, bank, over 250 kt below FL100.

plannedVsActual.title: Planned and actual
plannedVsActual.text: Fuel and times planned by SimBrief compared with what you actually flew.

community.title: You and the community

compareFlights.title: Compare two flights

sameAircraftComparison.title: Same aircraft

categoryTrends.title: Trends by category

phaseTime.title: Time per phase
phaseTime.text: Time spent taxiing, climbing, cruising and on approach, and how it changes.

goodPractices.title: Good practices
goodPractices.text: Flights without alerts, 250 kt below FL100, stabilised approaches, bank on approach: your rates.

export.title: CSV and PDF export

companies.title: Airlines
